<details>

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/installer/pull/10463):

>Adding an exponential backoff for making sure the storage account gets created properly and having the installer wait until it is done instead of erroring out for a "creating in progress" status return.


Instructions for interacting with me using PR comments are available [here](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/command-help?repo=openshift%2Finstaller).  If you have questions or suggestions related to my behavior, please file an issue against the [openshift-eng/jira-lifecycle-plugin](https://github.com/openshift-eng/jira-lifecycle-plugin/issues/new) repository.

## Walkthrough `CreateStorageAccount` now wraps Azure storage account creation in an exponential backoff retry loop; each attempt calls `BeginCreate` then `PollUntilDone`. Requests that return a conflict (operation in progress) are treated as transient and retried; other errors abort immediately. Error text on final failure was updated. ## Changes |Cohort / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Azure storage creation flow**
`pkg/infrastructure/azure/storage.go`|Added `wait.ExponentialBackoffWithContext`-based retry around storage account creation. Each retry invokes `BeginCreate` and `PollUntilDone`; `*azcore.ResponseError` with `StatusCode == http.StatusConflict` is treated as transient (logged and retried). Non-conflict errors abort. Final error message updated to "error creating storage account …".| ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 3 (Moderate) | ⏱️ ~22 minutes
✨ Finishing Touches
🧪 Generate unit tests (beta) - [ ] Create PR with unit tests

```
Inline comments:
In `@pkg/infrastructure/azure/storage.go`:
- Around line 153-157: The backoff config in the backoff variable disables
exponential growth and uses excessive jitter; update the backoff initialization
used by wait.ExponentialBackoffWithContext so Factor is 2 (to enable exponential
doubling) and Jitter is 0.2 (to limit randomization), keeping Duration and Steps
as-is; adjust only the backoff struct in pkg/infrastructure/azure/storage.go
(the backoff variable) that is passed to wait.ExponentialBackoffWithContext to
apply these values.
- Around line 167-181: Replace fragile string matching on createErr.Error() with
a typed Azure error check: where createErr is handled (the blocks around
createErr after the create call and after pollerResponse.PollUntilDone),
type-assert createErr to azcore.ResponseError (or check via errors.As) and
inspect the ErrorCode field for "StorageAccountOperationInProgress"; if it
matches, log the same message referencing in.StorageAccountName and
backoff.Duration and return false, nil, otherwise return the original createErr.
Update the two error-handling sites around the create call and
pollerResponse.PollUntilDone to use this pattern so retries rely on the typed
ResponseError.ErrorCode instead of strings.Contains(createErr.Error(), ...).
```

Proposed fix ```diff err = wait.ExponentialBackoffWithContext(ctx, backoff, func(ctx context.Context) (bool, error) { + isOperationInProgress := func(err error) bool { + var respErr *azcore.ResponseError + return errors.As(err, &respErr) && + respErr.StatusCode == http.StatusConflict && + respErr.ErrorCode == "StorageAccountOperationInProgress" + } + pollerResponse, createErr := accountsClient.BeginCreate( ctx, in.ResourceGroupName, in.StorageAccountName, accountCreateParameters, nil, ) if createErr != nil { - var respErr *azcore.ResponseError - if errors.As(createErr, &respErr) && respErr.StatusCode == http.StatusConflict { + if isOperationInProgress(createErr) { logrus.Infof("Storage account %s has an operation in progress, retrying in %s", in.StorageAccountName, backoff.Duration) return false, nil } return false, createErr } pollDoneResponse, createErr = pollerResponse.PollUntilDone(ctx, nil) if createErr != nil { - var respErr *azcore.ResponseError - if errors.As(createErr, &respErr) && respErr.StatusCode == http.StatusConflict { + if isOperationInProgress(createErr) { logrus.Infof("Storage account %s has an operation in progress, retrying in %s", in.StorageAccountName, backoff.Duration) return false, nil } return false, createErr } return true, nil }) ```

As per coding guidelines, "`**`: Focus on major issues impacting performance, readability, maintainability and security. Avoid nitpicks and avoid verbosity."
